summary: 研究者发现，打呵欠可能帮助调节脑部温度，还注意到它容易在旁人之间“传染”。影片和行为实验进一步探讨这种反应与共情、群体警觉的关系，这些解释仍属研究假说。
logic: 检验疲劳和生理调温解释
比较影片实验中的反应
提出群体警觉的进化假说

paragraphs.brief: 传染性哈欠背后的未知问题
sentences: While fatigue, drowsiness or boredom easily bring on yawns, scientists are discovering there is more to yawning than most people think.
疲劳、困倦或无聊固然容易使人打哈欠，但科学家正发现，打哈欠比多数人想象的更有内涵。
Not much is known about why we yawn or if it serves any useful function.
我们打哈欠的原因或它是否起到任何有益的作用，目前还不清楚。
People have already learned that yawning can be infectious.
人们已经知道打哈欠会传染

“Contagious yawning” is the increase in likelihood that you will yawn after watching or hearing someone else yawn, but not much is known about the underlying causes, and very little research has been done on the subject.
「传染性哈欠」指看见或听到别人打哈欠后，自己也更容易打哈欠；其背后原因了解得不多，相关研究也很少。
However, scientists at the University at Albany, as well as the University of Leeds and the University of London, have done some exploration.
然而，奥尔巴尼大学以及利兹大学和伦敦大学的科学家进行了一些探索。
paragraphs.gist: 疲倦或无聊容易引发哈欠，看见或听见他人打哈欠也会提高自己打哈欠的概率，但这种「传染」的原因与功能仍待解释。

paragraphs.brief: 冷敷和鼻呼吸支持大脑降温说
sentences: It is commonly believed that people yawn as a result of being sleepy or tired or because they need oxygen.
人们通常认为，人们因困困或疲劳或需要氧气而打哈欠。

However, the latest research shows that a yawn can help cool the brain and help it work more effectively, which is quite different from the popular belief that yawning promotes sleep and is a sign of tiredness.
然而，最新的研究表明，打哈欠可以帮助冷却大脑，帮助它更有效地工作，这与人们所认为的打哈欠能促进睡眠，是疲劳的表现，这大不相同。

Dr Andrew Gallup and his colleagues at the University at Albany in New York State said their experiments on 44 students showed that raising or lowering oxygen and carbon-dioxide levels in the blood did not produce that reaction.
安德鲁·盖洛普博士和他在纽约奥尔巴尼大学的同事说，他们对44名学生的实验表明，提高或降低血液中的氧气和二氧化碳含量并没有产生这种反应。
In the study, participants were shown videos of people laughing and yawning, and researchers counted how many times the volunteers responded to the “contagious yawns.”
实验让受试者观看别人微笑和打哈欠的录像，再统计志愿者有多少次被哈欠「传染」。
The researchers found that those who breathed through the nose rather than the mouth were less likely to yawn when watching a video of other people yawning.
研究人员发现，在观看别人打哈欠的视频时，那些通过鼻子而不是嘴呼吸的人更不会打哈欠。
The same effect was found among those who held a cool pack to their forehead, whereas those who held a warm pack yawned more while watching the video.
额头敷冷敷袋的受试者也较少跟着打哈欠，而敷温热袋观看视频的人打哈欠更多。
Since yawning occurs when brain temperature rises, sending cool blood to the brain serves to maintain optimal levels of mental efficiency.
由于打哈欠发生在大脑温度上升时，向大脑输送冷血有助于保持最佳的智力效率。
paragraphs.gist: 在四十四名学生的实验中，鼻呼吸或额头冷敷都减少了受哈欠感染的次数，这支持了哈欠可能帮助大脑降温、维持效率的解释。

paragraphs.brief: 自发哈欠与传染性哈欠的区别
sentences: Yawning is universal to humans and many animals.
打哈欠普遍见于人类和许多动物。
Cats, dogs and fish yawn just like humans do, but they yawn spontaneously.
猫、狗和鱼的哈欠就像人类一样但是它们自发地打哈欠
Only humans and chimpanzees, our closest relatives in the animal kingdom, have shown definite contagious yawning.
只有人类和黑猩猩动物王国最亲近的亲戚表现出了明显的传染性哈欠

Though much of yawning is due to suggestibility, sometimes people do not need to actually see a person yawn to involuntarily yawn themselves: hearing someone yawning or even reading about yawning can cause the same reaction.
打哈欠常受暗示影响，人却未必需要亲眼看见别人才会不自觉地跟着打：听见哈欠声，甚至读到有关文字，也可触发同样反应。
paragraphs.gist: 许多动物会自发打哈欠，但文中说只有人类和黑猩猩明确表现出传染性哈欠；对人来说，听见甚至读到哈欠也可能触发反应。

paragraphs.brief: 学生共情测试与传染性哈欠
sentences: However, contagious yawning goes beyond mere suggestibility.
然而，传染性的打哈欠不仅仅是暗示而已。
Recent studies show that contagious yawning is also related to our predisposition toward empathy — the ability to understand and connect with others’ emotional states.
近期研究表明，传染性哈欠还与共情倾向有关，即理解他人情绪状态并与之产生联系的能力。
So empathy is important, sure, but how could it possibly be related to contagious yawning?
所以同情很重要，当然，但怎么可能与传染性的打哈欠有关？
Psychologists at Leeds University in England set out to answer that.
英国利兹大学的心理学家开始回答这个问题。
In their study, researchers selected 40 psychology students and 40 engineering students.
研究人员在他们的研究中挑选了40名心理学学生和40名工程学学生。
Generally, psychology students are more likely to feel empathy for others, while engineering students are thought to be concerned with objects and science.
一般来说，心理学学生更可能同情他人，而工程学学生则被认为关心物体和科学。
Each student was made to wait individually in a waiting room along with an undercover assistant who yawned ten times in as many minutes.
每个学生分别在等候室里等待，身旁有一位未表明身份的研究助理，在十分钟内打十次哈欠。
The students were then given an emotional-quotient test: they were shown 40 images of eyes and asked what emotion each one displayed.
随后学生接受情商测试，观看四十张眼部图片，辨认每张图片呈现的情绪。
The results support the idea that contagious yawning is linked to empathy.
其结果支持了一种观点，即传染性的打哈欠与同情联系在一起。
The psychology students, whose future profession requires them to focus on others, yawned contagiously an average of 5.5 times in the waiting room and scored 28 out of 40 on the emotional test.
心理学学生未来的职业要求他们关注他人，这组人在等候室被传染打哈欠平均5.5次，情绪辨认平均得28分，满分40分。
The engineering students, who tend to focus on numbers and systems, yawned an average of 1.5 times and scored 25.5 out of 40.
往往关注数字和系统的工程学生平均被传染打哈欠1.5次，情绪辨认得25.5分，满分同为40分。
The difference does not sound large, but researchers consider it significant.
差距看起来不大，但研究者认为它有意义。
Strangely enough, women — generally viewed as more emotionally attuned — did not score any higher than men.
有趣的是，通常被认为更善于体察他人情绪的女性并未比男性得分更高。
paragraphs.gist: 利兹实验中，心理学学生比工程学生更常跟着打哈欠，也更善于从眼神辨认情绪，两项差异支持传染性哈欠与共情能力有关。

paragraphs.brief: 儿童观看两种片段后的不同反应
sentences: Another study, led by Atsushi Senju, a cognitive researcher at the University of London, also sought to answer that question.
由伦敦大学认知研究员Atsushi Senju领导的另一项研究也试图回答这个问题。
People with autism spectrum disorder are considered to be developmentally impaired emotionally: they have trouble connecting with others and find it difficult to feel empathy.
文中介绍的研究把自闭症谱系障碍与情绪发展方面的困难联系起来，认为部分人在与他人建立联系、感受共情时会遇到困难。
Since autistics have difficulty feeling empathy, they should not be susceptible to contagious yawning.
研究者据此推测，如果共情较困难，那么自闭症谱系组也应较不容易受到哈欠传染。
To find out, Senju and his colleagues placed 49 children aged 7 to 15 in a room with a television.
为了了解情况，Senju和他的同事将49名7至15岁的儿童安置在一个有电视机的房间里。
Twenty-four of the subjects had been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder; the other 25 were non-autistic.
其中24名儿童被诊断有自闭症谱系障碍，另外25名未被诊断有该障碍。
The children were shown short clips of people yawning as well as clips of people opening their mouths but not yawning.
向孩子们展示了人们打哈欠的短片，以及人们张开嘴但没有打哈欠的那些短片。
While the kids with autism showed the same lack of reaction to both kinds of clips, the non-autistic kids yawned more after the clips of people yawning.
谱系组儿童对两种片段都没有明显反应，另一组儿童看过打哈欠的片段后，自己打哈欠的次数则更多。
paragraphs.gist: 另一项研究让儿童看打哈欠或只张嘴的片段，未被诊断为自闭症的儿童在看哈欠后更常打哈欠，谱系组则未出现同样差异。

paragraphs.brief: 哈欠可能维持群体警觉与联系
sentences: There have also been studies suggesting that yawning, especially psychological “contagious” yawning, may have developed as a way of keeping a group of animals alert and bonding members of a group into a more unified one.
还有研究提出，打哈欠，尤其是心理上会「传染」的哈欠，可能是群居动物在演化中形成的机制，有助于群体保持警觉、加强成员之间的联系。
If an animal is drowsy or bored, it may not be as alert as it should be to spring into action, and its yawning is practically saying, “Hey, I need some rest; you stay awake.”
如果一只动物昏睡或无聊，它可能没有应有的警惕性去行动，而且它打哈欠实际上在说：“嘿，我需要休息，你保持清醒。”
Therefore, a contagious yawn could be an instinctual reaction to a signal from one member of the herd reminding the others to stay alert when danger comes.
因此，传染性的哈欠可能是对一个畜群成员发出的信号的本能反应，提醒其他人在危险到来时保持警惕。
Thus, the theory provides evidence that yawning comes from the evolution of early humans who needed to be ready to physically exert themselves at any given moment.
这种理论认为，早期人类需要随时准备采取耗费体力的行动，打哈欠可能正是在这种演化背景下形成的。
paragraphs.gist: 一种演化解释认为，传染性哈欠能传递群体成员需要休息的信号，提醒其他成员应对危险，也有助于维持整个群体的警觉和联系。

items.zh: 人类的想象力会导致打哈欠。
items.why: 题干说“想象也能让人打呵欠”。阅读只需在头脑中想象，恰好印证。

items.en: Research shows that yawning is closely related to occupations.
items.zh: 研究表明，打哈欠与职业密切相关。
items.why: 研究把“职业取向/专业"与打呵欠的频率做比较，说明职业 (occupation) 与打呵欠关联紧密。

items.en: An overview of the latest research on yawning.
items.zh: 关于打哈欠的最新研究概览。
items.why: A 段总览目前三所大学的最新探索，属于“最新研究概述”。

items.en: Yawning is used to regulate brain temperature.
items.zh: 打哈欠可用来调节大脑温度。
items.why: 脑温升高时会打哈欠，较凉的血液流向大脑，B段以此解释调节脑温的作用。

items.en: Scientists discovered some evidence disproving the earlier understanding of yawning.
items.zh: 科学家发现了一些证据，推翻了以往对打哈欠的解释。
items.why: 这组实验驳斥了“缺氧导致打呵欠"” 的旧观点，即“发现与原有理解相矛盾的证据”。

items.en: There is no gender difference in the cause of yawning.
items.zh: 引发打哈欠的原因并无性别差异。

items.en: People with certain disorders are less likely to be affected by other people yawning.
items.zh: 患有某些疾病的人较少受到别人打哈欠的影响。

items.en: Yawning is associated with the way people breathe.
items.zh: 打哈欠与人的呼吸方式有关。

items.en: People who are trained to feel empathy for others are more likely to yawn than those who are untrained.
items.zh: 与未受过训练的人相比，受过共情训练的人更容易打哈欠。

items.en: Another theory shows that yawning is used for ________ individuals into a tighter social unit.
items.zh: 另一种理论认为，打哈欠能把个体________在一起，形成更紧密的群体。
items.why: 用于凝聚成员成更紧密团体。

items.en: Alternatively, yawning can help increase alertness of group members in case ________ is close.
items.zh: 另有一种解释认为，当________临近时，打哈欠有助于提高群体成员的警觉性。
items.why: 增强警觉: 当危险临近。

items.en: For example, yawning signals that a member of the group needs some ________ and requires the others to stay aware of the surrounding situation.
items.zh: 例如，打哈欠表示一名成员需要________，其他成员则需要留意周围的情况。
items.why: 信号表明某成员需要休息。

items.en: This theory proves that yawning is only a spontaneous behaviour resulting from some part of a simple ________ system in early humans.
items.zh: 按这一理论，打哈欠只是早期人类某个简单的________系统所引发的自发行为。
items.why: 说明这只是一种源于早期人类的简单“警觉系统”。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 题干说“想象也能让人打呵欠”。阅读只需在头脑中想象，恰好印证。
用于凝聚成员成更紧密团体。
clauses: …, scientists are discovering there is more to yawning than most people think.
连接词 while 引出“While fatigue, drowsiness or boredom easily bring on yawns”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
“that people yawn as a result of being sleepy or tired or because they need oxygen”补足 believed 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 believed 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
vocabulary: 能在个体间传染般引发的
共情；体会他人感受的能力
